The maternal (systemic) NOEL is 25.00 mg/kg/day. The developmental (fetal) LOEL is 25.0 mg/kg/day based upon 1) decreased mean fetal weight & 2) retardation in skeletal development as evidenced by an increased number of litters with any variation & by decreased numbers of caudal vertebral & metacarpal ossification sites. The developmental (fetal) NOEL is 10.0 mg/kg/day. Evidence of treatment-related developmental toxicity consisted of decreased fetal viability, decreased fetal body weight, & increased incidence of fetal alterations, comprised, for the most part, of skeletal malformations & variations. A supplementary prenatal oral developmental toxicity study in rats confirmed the maternal & fetal findings of the previously conducted study & did not alter the study conclusions. Section.Description: Sorption to soils and sediments is an important factor on the transport and fate of organic contaminants in the environment.  The soil/water adsorption coefficient, also known as solid-water distribution coefficient (Kd), measures the amount of chemical substance adsorbed onto soil per amount of water.  Since adsorption occurs predominantly by partition into the soil organic matter, it is more useful to normalize the Kd value to the organic carbon content of a soil and express the distribution coefficient in Koc (organic carbon normalized distribution coefficient).  The greater the Kd (or Koc) value, the less likely a chemical will leach or contribute to runoff.  A very high value means it is strongly adsorbed onto soil and organic matter and does not move throughout the soil.
